small_guidance:
- Add larger tile configs tuned for M=N=K=8192/1024: try `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32/64` with `num_warps=8, num_stages=3/4`, and `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=32` variants; also drop `input_precision="ieee"` and use the default tf32 path (fp32 inputs on Ada allow tf32 `tl.dot` which roughly doubles tensor-core throughput, easily within 5e-2 tol).
- Since M=1024, N=8192, K=8192 are all multiples of 128, drop the K-tail masking by making the K-loop unconditional `tl.load` (no mask) — this removes per-iter mask compute; keep the M/N masks only.
- Increase `GROUP_M` sweep (try 4, 8, 16) for better L2 reuse on the 8×64 program grid, and consider a 2D launch grid `(num_pid_m, num_pid_n)` swizzled to avoid the modulo math.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a TF32 (or even fp16-accumulate-in-fp32 via on-the-fly cast) tiled GEMM — fp32 ieee `tl.dot` on a 4090 caps at ~40 TFLOPs vs ~165 TFLOPs for tf32; the 2.98 ms vs 2.43 ms gap is almost entirely tensor-core utilization.
- Consider a split-K or stream-K design: K=8192 is large and M=1024 only yields 8 row tiles at BLOCK_M=128, so the 4090's 128 SMs are under-occupied with a plain `(M/BM)*(N/BN)=64` grid — split-K (or stream-K) raises SM occupancy and lets the sigmoid/scale/residual epilogue run once at the end via an atomic-free two-pass or a stream-K reduction.
- Keep weight pre-transposed to (K, N) row-major (already done) so the inner-K loads on W are fully coalesced along N; ensure the epilogue (`sigmoid*scale + acc`) stays fused — do not split it out.
